comments.author: jguz1990
comments.body_html:
It seems the current version of the SOCOM mod is causing the game to softlock when using Insurance (the option hangs and never loads).

After testing, I found that the issue is due to a missing “insurance” section in the mod’s base.json file.

Adding the following snippet between “gridHeight” and “isAvailableInPVE” fixes the problem:

“gridHeight”: 150, “insurance”: { “availability”: false, “excluded_category”: [], “max_return_hour”: 0, “max_storage_time”: 99, “min_payment”: 0, “min_return_hour”: 0 }, “isAvailableInPVE”: true,

✅ Result: Game no longer softlocks when accessing Insurance. 🛠️ File: base.json 📍 Location: Between gridHeight and isAvailableInPVE

Posting this so others can patch it locally until an update officially resolves it.

comments.body_html:
Yes. Go to your SPT directory. Then navigate to “SPT\SP_Data\configs\core.json”

Edit the core.json with notepad and find these three lines and set them to “true”.

"removeModItemsFromProfile": true,

"removeInvalidTradersFromProfile": true,

"fixProfileBreakingInventoryItemIssues": true,

Then save the base.json and restart the server.

comments.author: felys
comments.body_html:
SOCOM Armory 3.0.3 — Bug: “AIAXMC338LM” trader offer references non-existent (wrong) item IDs

On server startup, SPT logs 4 warnings because items cannot be added to the item cache (they don’t exist in the item database):

Could not add 6917d89b54f5f109c106c1ee to cache, it does not exist in the item database! Could not add 6917d89b54f5f109c106c1ef to cache, it does not exist in the item database! Could not add 6917d89b54f5f109c106c1f2 to cache, it does not exist in the item database! Could not add 6917d89b54f5f109c106c1f4 to cache, it does not exist in the item database! Item: 6917d89b54f5f109c106c1ee lacks properties, cannot ascertain quality level, assuming 100% Item: 6917d89b54f5f109c106c1ef lacks properties, cannot ascertain quality level, assuming 100% Item: 6917d89b54f5f109c106c1f2 lacks properties, cannot ascertain quality level, assuming 100% Item: 6917d89b54f5f109c106c1f4 lacks properties, cannot ascertain quality level, assuming 100% Environment: SPT 4.0.13 (ASP.NET Core, SPT.Server.exe) / EFT client 0.16.9 / SOCOM Armory 3.0.3 (requires EpicsAIO / “EAIO” as prerequisite).

Root cause: The phantom items come from ONE bundled offer in user/mods/SOCOM/db/TraderSOCOM/assort.json:

_comment: AIAXMC338LM, offer _id: 6a65597f07cbba7f545fffd4 _tpl (weapon body) 6917d89b54f5f109c106c1ee child mod_barrel 6917d89b54f5f109c106c1ef child mod_stock 6917d89b54f5f109c106c1f2 child mod_handguard 6917d89b54f5f109c106c1f4 These four 6917d89b54f5f109c106c1xx IDs exist in NO database:

Not in base-game item templates (SPT_Data/database/templates/items.json). The base game DOES ship the AI AXMC .338 LM weapon — real _tpl is 627e14b21713922ded6f2c15 (weapon_accuracy_inernational_axmc_86x70). Not added by EpicsAIO (SOCOM’s prerequisite). EAIO adds AXMC barrels under db/CustomItems/AXMC_Barrels.json with IDs 8d5a67fd685ff05e7253b4f7 / 013114b6d9dc19eda4d0cad3 / a3a94608ed92771a766c6244 — a completely different ID range. Not in SOCOM’s own db/CustomItems/. So these 6917… IDs look like a copy-paste from a different mod’s ID scheme. The author clearly knew the correct IDs, because two sibling offers in the SAME assort.json work fine:

AIAXMC338LM2 → _tpl 627e14b21713922ded6f2c15 (real base-game AXMC weapon) — resolves OK AIAXMC338LM10round → _tpl 628120fd5631d45211793c9f (real 10-round magazine) — resolves OK Only AIAXMC338LM is stale.

I re-downloaded a fresh SOCOM 3.0.3 and confirmed the same issue (same 4 6917… IDs, still no such templates anywhere), so it’s a packaging bug in the release, not a corrupted download.

Impact: Server still starts and runs (cosmetic warnings only). The AIAXMC338LM offer is a phantom and can’t be purchased/loaded, but the AI AXMC .338 LM is still fully purchasable via the two working sibling offers, and all other SOCOM weapons are unaffected.

Suggested fix:

Point the offer at real IDs — replace the four 6917d89b54f5f109c106c1xx _tpl values in AIAXMC338LM with the actual AXMC item IDs (weapon body 627e14b21713922ded6f2c15; EAIO barrel 8d5a67fd…/013114b6…/a3a94608…; base-game stock/handguard); OR Remove the orphan AIAXMC338LM offer block (offer _id 6a65597f07cbba7f545fffd4 + its 3 child items) from assort.json, since the weapon is already covered by the two working sibling offers. Workaround I used: Deleted the phantom AIAXMC338LM offer block from assort.json. Verification: 0 unresolved _tpl remain across the whole SOCOM assort, and the two working AIAXMC offers are intact. Startup warnings are gone and the trader works normally.

comments.author: MT_Militia
comments.body_html:
I’ve literally been troubleshooting this all day and I’ve come up empty. I did change the mod load order as a test but I will need you to test it in your environment and see if it makes any impact if you are willing. Hit me up on Discord (mt_patriot1776) and I can give you a pre-release version of 3.0.4

Troubleshooting:

  • APBS patches BotLevelGenerator.GenerateBotLevel.
  • It reads BotGenerationDetails.PlayerLevel, supplied by SPT for the raid.
  • It calculates bot levels relative to that value using TierData.json.
  • SOCOM never writes to BotGenerationDetails, APBS’s RaidInformation, player Info.Level, experience, or prestige. The default APBS ranges themselves readily produce PMCs below level 10:
  • Player levels 1–10: bot range is effectively level 1 through player level +5.
  • Player levels 11–20: lower bound is player level −10.
  • Player levels 21–30: lower bound is player level −15.
  • Higher tiers use even larger downward deviations.
  • If the player is prestiged and enablePrestigeAnyLevel is enabled, APBS explicitly changes the permitted range to levels 1–79. Therefore, “almost all under 10” can be normal APBS output depending on the player level, prestige state, tier configuration, and sample size. The only shared profile boundary is SOCOMTraderUnlockSync.cs.

It:

  • Reads PmcData.Info.Level.

  • Initializes SOCOM trader information.

  • Updates SOCOM trader standing and loyalty.

  • Never assigns Info.Level, experience, or prestige.

  • SOCOM 2.x versions call LevelUp for the SOCOM trader directly. That change only narrows loyalty calculation to SOCOM. It does not change the player’s character level and does not feed APBS a different level.

  • One further interaction exists, but it concerns equipment rather than levels: APBS imports modded items at PostSptModLoader + 69. SOCOM registers its custom items earlier at PostDBModLoader + 3, so APBS can import SOCOM equipment into its bot pools. This can change what PMCs carry, but not their generated level.

Conclusion:

The claimed SOCOM → APBS level conflict is not supported by either project’s code. The most useful verification is to enable APBS debug logging and compare:
